meta.title: Cerveau Architecture
meta.description: Mapped from code (cmd/crv, internal/*, panel, sidecars, deploy): a Svelte panel, CLI and paired phone drive the Go core (:7700), which runs the agent loop against a Brain Core (llama.cpp or socket-activated vLLM), five memory stores, a guarded tool registry with RFX reflexes, and a front door (ignite + tailscale) that wakes the stack on demand.

nodes.label: Panel
nodes.note: panel/src — one SPA for desktop and phone; served embedded by the core.

nodes.label: crvcli
nodes.note: cmd/crvcli — no models, no state; talks to the running core.

nodes.label: Phone
nodes.note: android/ — PanelActivity wraps the panel; ScanActivity pairs; TEE-signed device key.

ports.shape: JSON: sessions, chat, memory, rfx, cores, cores/apply, cores/{id}/params, idle, devices, system/stats (every GPU)
turn events: tokens, tool calls, questions, errors

nodes.label: HTTP API
nodes.note: internal/api + internal/server. Bearer token + device signature on every remote request. Probes to the Core (health, /v1/models, modalities, window) carry CRV_MODEL_KEY — without it a vLLM Core behind VLLM_API_KEY read as nameless and the window stayed at the config fallback. Modalities: llama.cpp /props, else the Core's registry entry (VISION=1). Health syncs the window budget once the Core answered, so the panel shows the Core's real window before the first turn.

nodes.note: internal/loop — discussion / brainstorming / autopilot; breaker, retry, resume, progress, turn-boundary hooks (distill + semantic promotion).

nodes.label: Embed Sidecar
nodes.sublabel: Nemotron-3-Embed-1B · :8081 · on the 3060 under both TP=4 profiles, CPU otherwise
nodes.note: cerveau-embed.service reads ~/.config/cerveau/embed.env (EnvironmentFile=). Restart in the panel writes that file from the active Core's `embed` settings (profile embed.env → cores.json, user overrides in cores.d/<id>.embed.env) and the watchdog restarts the unit. BF16 profile: EMBED_DEVICE=cuda, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4 (the 3060, 3.7 GB), so recall runs at GPU speed and the four 3090s stay with the Core. Profiles without embed.env = CPU, the one-GPU default.

nodes.label: Wake-on-request socket
nodes.note: deploy/idle — crv-core-vllm-proxy.socket is installed and listening; cores.json points here, so whether vLLM is loaded is systemd's problem.

nodes.label: vLLM core
nodes.sublabel: W4A16 core · :18021 · 98K ctx · fp8 KV · single 3090
nodes.note: Profile-less original Core (unit crv-core-vllm.service, given a `unit` in cores.json by hand). ~/qwen-serving/single-user/start_qwen.sh with MAX_LEN=98304, GPU_UTIL=0.90, DRAFT_TOKENS=0. 179,443 KV tokens at the 96K window. Parked with its socket down while the BF16 Core is active; the watchdog switch handles the GPU 0 overlap.

nodes.label: cores.json
nodes.note: ~/.config/cerveau/cores.json — a Core is a whole runtime behind one OpenAI-compatible URL. Since 2026-09-04 each profile entry also carries `params`: the unit's Environment= lines, the defaults the panel shows and the user can override (cores.d).

ports.shape: any request → wake stack → proxy to :7700

nodes.label: ignite
nodes.note: sidecars/ignite — serves a 'waking' page while the core boots.

nodes.label: systemd --user
nodes.sublabel: cerveau · cerveau-embed · cerveau-llama · crv-core-vllm · crv-core-vllm-27b-bf16 · crv-core-vllm-27b-w8a16

nodes.label: Park watchdog
nodes.sublabel: parks Cores on request · switches Cores on request
nodes.note: deploy/idle/crv-park-watchdog.sh — outside the core process so a crash can never strand the machine. Park: stop every crv-core-*.service (CRV_CORE_UNITS from the profiles.conf drop-in), never a socket. Switch: stop every OTHER Core's unit, proxy AND socket, start the chosen socket, `systemctl restart` the chosen unit (restart, not start: on the already-active Core that is how new parameters are applied), restart the embedder if embed.env changed, restart cerveau.service. Progress to switch-status.json.

nodes.label: Web
nodes.ack: The frame is literally named Outside the machine — it groups what is beyond the boundary rather than claiming ownership, and leaving the node unframed made it float with no explanation of why it was apart

nodes.label: vLLM BF16 Core
nodes.sublabel: Qwen3.8-27B BF16 · TP=4 · 262K · bf16 KV · vision · prefix cache · :18031
nodes.note: Profile qwen3.8-27b-bf16-tp4 (core id vllm-27b-bf16). Launcher ~/Documents/GitHub/Gpu-Rig/quad/start_qwen_bf16_tp4.sh. Nothing approximated: bf16 weights, bf16 KV, vision tower loaded, MTP 3 (lossless), PREFIX_CACHE=1 (vLLM's default for this hybrid is off; 14k-token prefix TTFT 5.9 s → 0.39 s). Measured 2026-09-04: 13.07 GiB weights/GPU, KV pool ~371k tokens (1.41× a 262K request), 92 tok/s decode, 1280×800 image = 1034 tokens in 1.2 s, GPU_UTIL 0.88 (0.92 OOMed on rank 0). Cold start ~2 min, warm ~40 s. Needs all four 3090s.

nodes.label: Wake-on-request socket
nodes.note: Same pattern as :18020, one pair of ports per profile. cores.json entry vllm-27b-bf16 points here.

nodes.label: cores.d overrides
nodes.note: Per-Core runtime parameters the user changed in Settings → Engine → Profile (KV, VISION, MAX_LEN, GPU_UTIL…). Only the diff from the profile; reset removes the file. The Core unit reads it through EnvironmentFile= at its next start, so a change applies on park/wake or restart and never reaches a running engine. PORT refused.

nodes.label: Profile installer
nodes.sublabel: deploy/profiles/ — install.sh, one dir per Core, ENGINE-PATCHES.md
nodes.note:
Each profile is one Brain Core made installable: core.json + the three units + embed.env. install.sh copies them, enables only the socket, merges the core.json entry and rebuilds the watchdog's unit list.

The two TP=4 profiles have their own standalone diagrams — profile-w8a16-tp4 and profile-bf16-tp4 — so this node stays a single box here.

ENGINE-PATCHES.md records the eight vLLM patches and which one gates PREFIX_CACHE=1.

nodes.label: Switch request + status
nodes.note: The panel's Restart button. POST /api/cores/apply writes switch-request.json {core, unit, stop[], restart_cerveau, restart_embed} and ~/.config/cerveau/embed.env; the park watchdog consumes it and writes switch-status.json (queued → stopping → starting → restarting → done | failed), which /api/cores exposes as `switch` for the panel to poll. tmpfs: a stale request cannot survive a reboot.

nodes.label: vLLM W8A16 Core
nodes.sublabel: Qwen3.8-27B W8A16 + MTP · TP=4 · 262K · fp8 KV · vision · prefix cache · :18041
nodes.note:
The active Core as of 2026-09-04. int8 weights (compressed-tensors, group-128, symmetric) with the vision tower, lm_head, MTP head and GDN gates left in BF16, so the marlin int8 kernels engage. 7.49 GiB of weights per rank leaves 12.7 GiB of KV: 1,493,666 tokens, 5.70x concurrency at the full 262k window.

Prefix caching is ON and only safe because vllm#48375 is applied — see the enginepatches node. Without that patch it must be 0.

nodes.label: vLLM patches
nodes.sublabel: ~/qwen-serving/patches/*.patch — 8 vendored, applied to the installed package
nodes.note:
Applied to site-packages, not a source checkout: nothing in the venv records that they are applied, so they must be re-applied after any pip install, upgrade or venv rebuild.

vllm-pr48375-mamba-prefix-eagle.patch GATES a setting: PREFIX_CACHE=1 is only safe with it. MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit ignored drop_eagle_block, so a cached page whose recurrent-state snapshot was taken over REJECTED MTP draft tokens could be reused — silently wrong tool calls and long-context output, never an error.

vllm-pr50021-gdn-spec-bounds.patch bounds accepted-token lookups in the GDN spec-decode kernels; without it several concurrent MTP requests raise cudaErrorIllegalAddress.

Documented in deploy/profiles/ENGINE-PATCHES.md.
